items.title: Dyna-2 Proves Scaling Laws for Robotics: 1 Million Hours of Human Video Unlocks Zero-Shot Dexterity
items.summary: Dyna-2, a world-action model pre-trained on over one million hours of human video data, demonstrates a human-to-robot transfer scaling law, proving that scaling human video predictably improves zero-shot performance on unseen robot hardware. The model achieved an 87% pass rate in real-world zero-shot deployments, outperforming its Vision-Language-Action predecessor, Dyna-1. Dyna-2's architecture relies on "video co-training" and introduces a novel one-step video generation distillation pipeline to reduce inference latency by two orders of magnitude.
items.audio_script:
From Humanoids Daily, "Dyna-2 Proves Scaling Laws for Robotics: 1 Million Hours of Human Video Unlocks Zero-Shot Dexterity". Dyna-2 has demonstrated a human-to-robot transfer scaling law, proving that scaling human video predictably improves zero-shot performance on unseen robot hardware. The model achieved an 87% pass rate in real-world zero-shot deployments, outperforming its predecessor, Dyna-1, and marking a significant milestone in robotics research.

Dyna-2 was pre-trained on over one million hours of human video data using the "video co-training" method, where the model is trained in parallel with humans performing actions to be replicated by robots. This approach enables the model to learn from human interactions and adapt to new robot hardware with unprecedented flexibility. The novel architecture also introduced a one-step video generation distillation pipeline, significantly reducing inference latency.

The achievement showcases Dyna-2's capabilities as a pioneering solution for robotics and highlights its potential to unlock zero-shot dexterity in robots.

items.title: PlusAI reaches ‘93.4 percent safety readiness’ ahead of autonomous truck launch
items.summary: PlusAI has reached 93.4 percent Safety Case Readiness, ahead of its planned commercial launch of factory-built driverless trucks in 2027. The company's Autonomous Miles Percentage increased to 99.8 percent, and Remote Assistance Free Trips rose to 85.2 percent during the first half of 2026. PlusAI expects to reach 100 percent Safety Case Readiness by 2027 and is targeting over 90 percent of trips without remote assistance at commercial launch.

items.title: Electronic skin gives robots and prosthetics ‘human-like touch sensing’
items.summary: Researchers at Hanyang University ERICA have developed a vertically integrated dual-gated tribotronic transistor architecture that offers tuneable sensitivity, reliable contact and proximity detection, and minimal pixel footprint for high-density array integration. This technology can pave the way for electronic skin systems that allow robots and prosthetics to reliably perceive human touch. The device exhibits stable response and recovery times of 127 and 212 milliseconds during each contact-separation cycle, making it suitable for applications in healthcare robots, health monitoring, and autonomous systems.

items.title: A ‘5-in-1’ seed-sized surgical robot
items.summary: Scientists at Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, have developed a seed-sized surgical robot that can navigate soft and uneven surfaces to perform five surgical functions wirelessly, including cutting biological tissues, releasing drugs, gripping tissue samples, and generating heat remotely. The robot, measuring 4.4 mm in length, uses magnetic coils and soft magnetic materials to control its movements and switch between different functions in under a second. Testing on biological tissues revealed that the robot was able to perform the specified functions with minimal damage or adverse effects.
items.audio_script:
From Robohub, "A ‘5-in-1’ seed-sized surgical robot" reports on scientists at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore who have developed a revolutionary new device. The researchers created a tiny surgical robot that can perform five distinct functions wirelessly on soft and uneven surfaces, including cutting biological tissues, releasing drugs, gripping tissue samples, and generating heat remotely.

The robot, measuring just 4.4 mm in length, utilizes magnetic coils and soft magnetic materials to control its movements and switch between different functions within a mere second. To test the device's capabilities, the researchers employed biological tissues, revealing minimal damage or adverse effects during the performance of the specified functions. This breakthrough demonstrates the immense potential for miniaturized robots in surgical procedures.

This innovation could significantly advance the field of robotics and artificial intelligence, paving the way for more efficient and precise medical treatments with miniature devices that can navigate complex surfaces with unprecedented precision.

items.title: Robot Recycler Salvages Parts from Broken Machines
items.summary: Researchers at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology have designed a system to predictively disassemble broken robots, salvaging valuable parts while protecting them from damage. The system uses a predictive algorithm and robotic manipulators to break down the robot, with updates made based on observations. The goal is to create a circular economy where old devices are repurposed to make new ones, reducing waste.
items.audio_script:
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Robot Recycler Salvages Parts from Broken Machines." Researchers at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology have designed a system that enables predictive disassembly of broken robots, resulting in salvaged valuable parts without causing damage. The system employs a predictive algorithm and robotic manipulators to break down the robot, with updates made based on observations and real-time data analysis. This innovative approach aims to create a circular economy where old devices are repurposed to make new ones, reducing electronic waste.

The system's methodology involves collecting data from the broken robot and feeding it into the predictive algorithm, which then determines the most efficient disassembly sequence to minimize part loss and damage. The robotic manipulators execute the plan, carefully disassembling the robot while preserving critical components. This process is repeated in real-time, allowing for continuous monitoring of the system's performance.

This breakthrough technology has significant implications for the AI and tech industry, as it paves the way for the development of more efficient and sustainable device recycling practices. As this field continues to evolve, expect to see further innovations in robotic disassembly and repair methods, ultimately driving towards a more circular and environmentally conscious approach to electronic waste management.

items.title: Interview with Maximo’s Nick Hegeman: 180,000 robotic installations of solar panels and counting
items.summary: Maximo, an AI-powered robotic system developed by AES, has now installed over 180,000 solar panels representing more than 100 MW of generating capacity. The robots using Maximo have exceeded 500 installations per day, while crews using the technology can install up to 24 modules per person per shift hour. Nick Hegeman, chief commercial officer for Maximo, attributes customer adoption to the ease of integration and reliable performance, which has taken robotics from an unproven technology to a practical construction tool.

From Robotics & Automation News, "Interview with Maximo’s Nick Hegeman: 180,000 robotic installations of solar panels and counting." This story reports on the rapid adoption of Maximo's AI-powered robotic system in the construction industry, particularly for installing solar panels.

This milestone marks significant progress in the adoption of AI-powered robotic systems in the construction industry, showcasing their potential for increased efficiency and productivity.

items.title: Generalizing deep reinforcement learning across cable-driven parallel robot configurations with actuator-level policies
items.summary: Researchers at CRAN and LARSEN introduce a novel deep reinforcement learning approach for controlling cable-driven parallel robots (CDPRs) that does not depend on the specific robot configuration. The method trains an actuator-level policy, which controls each motor to achieve its target cable length, instead of traditional methods that learn to control the entire robot. This approach offers two main advantages: a single shared policy can be applied to any CDPR configuration, regardless of actuator count, and reliance on inverse kinematics avoids the more challenging forward kinematics problem.

items.title: SC$^{2}$-WM: A Self-Correcting World Model with Closed-Loop Feedback for Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments
items.summary: SC$^{2}$-WM proposes a self-correcting world model framework with internal feedback for closed-loop decision making in Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments (VLN-CE). The method derives feedback from world-model foresight to refine state-level plans before action execution. Conditional world-aware adaptation is introduced to selectively update the world model at test time when feedback indicates model capacity insufficiency, improving navigation robustness and generalization in experiments on standard VLN-CE benchmarks.

items.title: Self Supervised Learning from Automatically Generated Demonstrations for Visual Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: A self-supervised visual manipulation method learns relative pose corrections directly from wrist-mounted RGB images, generating demonstrations around a target pose without requiring explicit camera to robot extrinsic calibration. The proposed pipeline uses ROS 2 and Isaac Sim to collect labeled image-pose pairs, training a convolutional network to regress relative translation and rotation from single frame observations. In simulation and real-world experiments, the system performs end-to-end grasp attempts with success rates of 66.6% and 63.6%, showing potential for practical visual manipulation with limited setup effort.

items.title: AeroDPO: Unleashing Lightweight UAV Navigation with High-Fidelity Perception and Automated Preference Optimization
items.summary: A lightweight 2B model equipped with high-fidelity visual inputs successfully matches the overall success rates of massive 7B baselines in Vision-Language Navigation for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV-VLN). However, this minimalist policy exposes a fundamental robustness flaw inherent to pure Behavior Cloning (BC), leading to alarming collision rates. AeroDPO, a zero-cost automated Direct Preference Optimization pipeline, is proposed to overcome this vulnerability by leveraging deterministic physical simulation state rollback and offline vision language inspection. This approach boosts success rates to 49.16% on unmapped scenarios while drastically suppressing collision rates.

items.title: Learning Physical Interaction: A Survey of Tactile- and Force-aware Robot Learning
items.summary: The survey "Learning Physical Interaction: A Survey of Tactile- and Force-aware Robot Learning" proposes a unified hierarchical structure, TF-ART, to map individual methods into a single framework that captures multimodal sensing and multi-phase system design in force- and tactile-aware robot learning. The study characterizes how recent works organize observation modalities, encode and fuse heterogeneous sensory inputs, generate and refine actions across multiple phases, and connect learned policies to reactive robot-end control.

items.title: Projection-Retraction MPPI: Exact Constraint-Manifold Control for Manipulators
items.summary: MPPI control handles constraints only through cost, which can lead to inaccurate results. Projection-Retraction MPPI (PR-MPPI) proposes an exact constraint-manifold control for manipulators by projecting sampled velocity to satisfy both equality and inequality constraints. This projection ensures that the returned command satisfies the closed-chain equality to numerical tolerance. PR-MPPI has been validated on 14-DoF dual-arm systems, including a joint-limit stress test and randomized obstacle avoidance.

items.title: Reconfigurable Structural Robotic Assembly: Interlocking 3D Aggregations with Self-Aligning Compound Nested Lattice Modules
items.summary: Researchers have developed self-aligning compound nested lattice modules composed of conjoined cuboctahedral-octahedral units for robotic construction. The modules enable interlocking aggregation along the x, y, and z axes and can be disassembled and reused across different configurations. Compression testing showed a stiffness of 4,556 N/mm, a maximum load of 3,445 N, and a compressive modulus of 17.5 MPa. The system was demonstrated through furniture and architectural scale structures assembled using robotic arms and mobile assemblers.

items.title: AdaDexGrasp: Adaptive Dexterous Grasping via 3D Visuo-Tactile Representation Fusion
items.summary: A unified visuo-tactile-fusion grasping framework, AdaDexGrasp, integrates grasp generation, feasibility prediction, and adaptive refinement to achieve stable and adaptive grasps. The method introduces an efficient visuo-tactile representation that associates tactile signals with finger identities, supporting contact-aware grasp pose generation during planning and tactile-guided refinement after contact. This approach enhances grasp success rates and generalization across diverse objects in simulation and real-world environments.
